weeks.title: Q3: W1 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to explain fraction equivalence using a strip diagram and the number line, and relate that to the use of multiplication and division.
sc: I can use a strip diagram and number line to find equivalent fractions for halves, fourths, and eighths.
I can use a number line, multiplication, and division to decompose and compose fractions.
I can decompose a non-unit fraction using a number line and division.

days.lo: I am learning how to reason using benchmarks to compare two fractions on thenumber line.
sc: I can reason about the size of a fraction compared to ½
I can plot points on a number line by thinking about fractions in relation to 0, ½  , or 1 and compare the fractions.
I can use the benchmarks 0, ½ , and 1 to compare two fractions without using a number line.

days.lo: I am learning how to find common units or the number of units to compare two fractions.
sc: I can reason about fraction size using unit language.
I can compare fractions with related numerators.
I can compare fractions having related denominators where one denominator is a factor of the other.
I can compare fractions using different methods of reasoning.

days.lo: I am learning how to use visual models to add and subtract two fractions with the same units, including subtracting from one whole.
sc: I can model subtract a fraction from 1 using a number line.
I can use a number bond or strip diagrams to subtract a fraction from a number between 1 and 2.

weeks.title: Q3: W2 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to add and subtract more than two fractions.
sc: I can model a strategy to solve addition and subtraction of fractions.
I can justify solutions to addition and subtraction problems with fractions.

days.lo: I am learning how to add a fraction less than 1 to, or subtract a fraction less than 1 from, a whole number using decomposition and visual models.
sc: I can add a fraction less than 1 to a whole number using a strip diagram.
I can subtract a fraction less than 1 from a whole number using a strip diagram.
I can form fact family facts given three related numbers.
I can subtract a fraction less than 1 from a whole number using decomposition.

days.lo: I am learning how to decompose and compose fractions greater than 1 to expressthem in various forms.
sc: I can rename fractions as mixed numbers using decomposition with number bonds.
I can rename fractions as mixed numbers using a number line.

days.lo: I am learning how to compare fractions greater than 1 by reasoning using benchmark fractions.
sc: I can compare mixed numbers and fractions on a number line using benchmark fractions.
I can compare two mixed numbers or two fractions greater than 1.

days.lo: I am learning how to compare fractions greater than 1 by creating common numerators or denominators.
sc: I can model, using a strip diagram, the comparison of two mixed numbers having related denominators.
I can compare two fractions with unrelated denominators.
I can compare two fractions.

weeks.title: Q3: W3 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to solve word problems with dot plots.
sc: I can create a dot plot to show the information.
I can interpret the information on a dot plot using factual statements.
I can solve word problems using information presented on a dot plot

days.lo: I am learning how to add a mixed number and a fraction.
sc: I can use unit form and the number line to add a mixed number and a fraction having sums of fractional units less than or equal to 1.
I can complete a unit of one to add a mixed number and a fraction.
I can decompose a sum of a mixed number and a fraction with sums of fractional units greater than 1.
I can decompose a fractional addend to make one before finding the sum.

days.lo: I am learning how to add mixed numbers.
sc: I can add mixed numbers combining like units.
I can add mixed numbers when the sum of the fractional units is greater than 1 by combining like units.
I can add mixed numbers when the sum of the fractional units is greater than 1 by making one.
I can record the addition of mixed numbers.

days.lo: I am learning how to subtract a fraction from a mixed number.
sc: I can subtract a fraction from a mixed number by counting back.
I can subtract a fraction less than 1 from a whole number by decomposing the subtrahend.
I can decompose the total to take out 1 when subtracting a fraction from a mixed number when there are not enough fractional units.

weeks.title: Q3: W4 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to subtract a mixed number from a mixed number.
sc: I can subtract a mixed number from a mixed number by counting up.
I can subtract a mixed number from a mixed number when there are not enough fractional units by first subtracting the whole numbers and then decomposing the subtrahend.
I can Subtract a mixed number from a mixed number when there are not enough fractional units by decomposing a whole number into fractional parts.

weeks.title: Q3: W5 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to use metric measurement to model the decomposition of one whole into tenths.
sc: I can compose and decompose 1 kilogram, representing tenths in fraction form and decimal form.
I can decompose 1 meter, representing tenths in fraction form and decimal form.
I can decompose 1 centimeter, representing tenths in fraction form and decimal form.

days.lo: I am learning how to use metric measurement and area models to represent tenthsas fractions greater than 1 and decimal numbers.
sc: I can draw line segments of given lengths, and express each segment as a mixed number and a decimal.
I can use the area model to represent tenths as fractions greater than 1 and as decimal numbers.

days.lo: I am learning how to represent mixed numbers with units of tens, ones, and tenthswith place value disks, on the number line, and in expanded notation.
sc: I can make groups of 10 tenths to rename as ones. Write the number in decimal form.
I can represent mixed numbers with units of tens, ones, and tenths in expanded notation.
I can use place value disks to explore 1 tenth as much.
I can use the number line to model mixed numbers with units of ones and tenths.

days.lo: I am learning how to use meters to model the decomposition of one whole into hundredths. Represent and count hundredths.
sc: I can recognize 1 centimeter as 1/100 of a meter, which can be written as 1/100m and as 0.01 m.
I can name hundredths as tenths and some hundredths, stating the number in fraction and decimal form.

weeks.title: Q3: W6 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to model the equivalence of tenths and hundredths using the areamodel and place value disks.
sc: I can simplify hundredths by division.
I can model hundredths with an area model.
I can compose hundredths to tenths using place value disks, and then represent with a number bond.
I can use place value disks to represent a decimal fraction. Write the equivalent decimal in unit form.

days.lo: I am learning how to use the area model and number line to represent mixed numbers with units of ones, tenths, and hundredths in fraction and decimalforms.
sc: I can represent mixed numbers with units of ones, tenths, and hundredths using area models.
I can represent mixed numbers with units of ones, tenths, and hundredths on a number line.
I can match the unit form of a mixed number to its decimal and fraction forms.

days.lo: I am learning how to model mixed numbers with units of hundreds, tens, ones,tenths, and hundredths in expanded notation and on the place value chart.
sc: I can use place value disks to model mixed numbers with units of hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, and hundredths on the place value chart.
I can say the value of each digit.
I can express a decimal number in decimal and fraction expanded notation.
days.note: Combined lesson: Lesson 7 combined with Lesson 8 Concept Development

days.lo: I am learning how to use the place value chart and metric measurement to compare decimals and answer comparison questions.
sc: I can compare pairs of decimal numbers representing length.
I can compare pairs of decimal numbers representing mass.
I can compare pairs of decimal numbers representing volume.

days.lo: I am learning how to use area models and the number line to compare decimalnumbers, and record comparisons using < , > , and = .
sc: I can compare pairs of decimal numbers using an area model. Record the comparison using < , > , and = .
I can compare decimal numbers on a number line. Record the comparison using < , > , and = .
I can compare decimal numbers using < , > , and = .

weeks.title: Q3: W7 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to apply place value understanding to add tenths and hundredths.
sc: I can use place value disks to model units of hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, and hundredths on the place value chart.
I can use zeros to keep the value of the unit.
I can use the standard algorithm to add and sub tenths and hundredths.

days.lo: I am learning how to apply place value understanding to add tenths and hundredths.
sc: I can use place value disks to model units of hundreds, tens, ones, tenths, and hundredths on the place value chart.
I can use zeros to keep the value of the unit.
I can use the standard algorithm to add and sub tenths and hundredths.

days.lo: I am learning how to solve word problems involving the addition and subtraction ofmeasurements in decimal form.
sc: I can model the problem.
I can calculate to solve and write a statement.
I can assess the solution for reasonableness.

weeks.title: Q3: W8 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to express money amounts given in various forms as decimalnumbers.
sc: I can express pennies, dimes, and quarters as fractional parts of a dollar.
I can express the total value of combinations of pennies, dimes, and quarters in fraction and decimal form.
I can find the sum of two sets of bills and cents using whole number calculations and unit form

days.lo: I am learning how to solve word problems, including the calculation of profit & and the difference between fixed and variable expenses.
sc: I can define profit
I can determine profit.
I can describe ways to spend and save money.
I can reason about the advantages and disadvantages of saving and spending.
I can define fixed and variable expenses

days.lo: I am learning how to create conversion tables for length, weight, and capacity unitsusing measurement tools, and use the tables to solve problems.
sc: I can relate pounds to ounces using a scale.
I can relate meters to feet using meter sticks and rulers
I can relate feet to inches using rulers.

days.lo: I am learning how to create conversion tables for length, weight, and capacity unitsusing measurement tools, and use the tables to solve problems.
sc: I can relate gallons to quarts.
I can relate quarts to pints. Relate pints to gallons.
I can relate pints to cups. Relate cups to quarts and gallons.
I can calculate a two step conversion.

weeks.title: Q3: W8 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to create conversion tables for units of time, and use the tables tosolve problems.
sc: I can convert minutes to seconds.
I can convert hours to minutes.
I can convert days to hours.
I can solve a word problem involving converting days to hours.

days.lo: I am learning how to solve multiplicative comparison word problems usingmeasurement conversion tables.
sc: I can model the problem.
I can calculate to solve, and write a statement.
I can assess the solution.

days.lo: I am learning how to solve problems involving mixed units of capacity.
sc: I can add mixed units of capacity.
I can subtract mixed units of capacity.

days.lo: I am learning how to solve problems involving mixed units of length.
sc: I can add mixed units of length.
I can subtract mixed units of length.

days.lo: I am learning how to solve problems involving mixed units of weight.
sc: I can add mixed units of weight measure, and share alternate strategies.
I can subtract units of weight measure when there are not enough smaller units.
